entries.reason: MPSImageIntegral.h:31 annotates the class ios(9.0), and MPSImageIntegral.h:19-20 states the rectangle exactly: sumRect.origin = MPSUnaryImageKernel.offset, sumRect.size = dest_position - MPSUnaryImageKernel.clipRect.origin. The value at a destination position is therefore the sum of the source over that rectangle, which is a prefix sum this port computes on the CPU. The class declares no member of its own - MPSImageIntegral.h:33-35 is @end straight after the @interface - so the initializer is MPSUnaryImageKernel's and the encode is the object's, on MPSImage9.m. Measured 2026-09-30 on this host by tests/backports/host/mpsimage9/run.sh: 9 cases over 1x1, 3x2 and 5x5 images, 96 elements COMPARED 0 MISMATCHES, and both planted builds are caught (96/96 and 9/9). Every value is this port's own answer against a plain C reference written from the wording above, in the same process: host MPS cannot be the oracle here, this host's AGX family lacking computeCommandEncoderWithDispatchType: and the release's own kernel dying on encode. No number on this row measures Apple's code
entries.effect: the sum of the source over the rectangle from the offset to the destination position, per channel, inclusive of the destination position itself - MPSImageIntegral.h:19-20 states the size as a difference of two POSITIONS rather than a count, so a rectangle that size holds one more sample per axis than its length. Computed in double through the walking layer (MPSImageWalk13.m) and stored at the destination's own element width. The kernel's offset is honoured as {0,0,0}, the header's default at MPSImageKernel.h:131-138; a caller who set a non-zero offset is answered against the origin and that path is owed MEASURED, and not against the release's own kernel: the oracle is a CPU reference in the port's own process, computed from the header formulas above, because this host's AGX family does not implement computeCommandEncoderWithDispatchType: and the release's own MPSImage kernels die encoding. entries.effect: Y = X / L^beta with L = delta + alpha/N * sum over q in Q(k) of X^2, NORMALIZED ACROSS NEARBY FEATURE CHANNELS with no spatial extent, per MPSCNNNormalization.h:379-387. The defaults are alpha 1.0, beta 5.0, delta 1.0 and kernelSize 5 (:397-413), all MEASURED on a fresh kernel; kernelSize is READONLY there, so the initialiser is its only setter. The divisor is the kernelSize and NOT the window's length: MEASURED with kernelSize 3 the implied divisor is 3.000000 at every output checked. Q(k) = [max(0, k-floor(N/2)), min(D-1, k+floor((N-1)/2))] is ASYMMETRIC, so with four channels and N=3 the first channel sees three and the last sees two

entries.effect: Y = pm + ps*(X - p0*M) / (delta + alpha*VAR)^beta per MPSCNNNormalization.h:139-142, over a CENTRED kw x kw window of one feature channel with the off-image value ZERO and VAR = E[x^2] - M^2. Every default is MEASURED on a fresh kernel and agrees with :151-178 to the digit: alpha 0.0, beta 0.5, delta 1/1024, p0 1.0, pm 0.0, ps 1.0. The header says alpha 0 is "not recommended and is preserved for backwards compatibility" and that with alpha 0 "it performs a local mean subtraction", which is what the measured top case is. p0 = 1 IS LOAD-BEARING and the measurement settles it: at alpha 0 the denominator is the constant delta^beta, so the release's answer solves M = X - Y*delta^beta, and at (0,0) that is 1.55555558 against the centred 3x3 mean 1.55555556. With p0 = 0 the answer at (0,0) would be 32 where the release answers -17.7777786

entries.effect: Y = X / (delta + alpha/(kw*kh) * N2)^beta per MPSCNNNormalization.h:26-28, where N2 is the sum of the squares of a CENTRED kw x kw window of ONE feature channel, the denominator divides by the window's AREA, and what falls outside the image is ZERO. THE WINDOW IS CENTRED and that is measured, not read: at kw=3, where a centred window (first = -1) and a backward one (first = -2) are different windows, the release agrees with centred to 3.0e-06 and disagrees with backward by 7.7e+04. An earlier version of this row claimed an EVEN kernel's window reaches back, on the strength of a kw=2 case - and for a 2-wide kernel a centred window starts at -1 and a backward one at -1 as well, so that case could not tell the two rules apart and proved nothing; the claim is withdrawn and the kw=3 and kw=5 cases are what the row rests on

entries.reason: CARRIED, and the two measurements on this row are why no number in it is a measurement of Apple's code. The host's own MPSImagePyramid CRASHES on this encode: run against the system's own MPS on an 8x8 R32Float texture with four mip levels, encodeToCommandBuffer:inPlaceTexture:fallbackCopyAllocator: takes the process down with SIGSEGV, exit 139 (transcript .agent-work/runs/host/mpsr10/pyramid.txt, built and run by tests/backports/host/mpscnn10's sibling pyramid.m). The release therefore cannot be compared against here, and nothing in MPSImagePyramid10.m claims to match it. Seen from this port the same gap is that MPSImage13.m:253 makes every texture with mipmapped:NO, so there are no mip levels for such a fill to write into at all. That is why this class's encode is refused unless the caller's texture has the levels to write into, and refuses a texture with fewer than two. MEASURED 2026-10-01 on this host (Apple M4 Pro, macOS 27.0): every one of this slice's classes RESOLVES in the system's own MetalPerformanceShaders, and MPSCNNNeuronReLU encodes and writes - so the sentence this row used to carry, "host MPS cannot run here: this host's AGX family lacks computeCommandEncoderWithDispatchType:", is FALSE here and the host's MPS is the oracle for every number below. entries.reason: the class EXISTS and its five declared members ANSWER - MPSImage.h:927-1010 declares the class over MPSImage with +defaultAllocator (:930), +temporaryImageWithCommandBuffer:imageDescriptor: (:938-947) and the two texture-descriptor forms (:955-995), and MPSImageElements10.m defines all five - and nothing in the port APPLIES the one thing it exists for, which is the RECYCLING. MPSImage.h:941-946 says the texture "will become invalid before this time due to the action of the readCount property", and MPSImage.h:1030-1050 puts that decision in an MPSImageAllocator: a protocol this port does not carry, and which MPSImage.h:236-238 makes NSSecureCoding. Every MPS kernel here walks an MPSImage's values on the CPU - MPSImage13.m holds them in a texture it reads - so the release's GPU-private texture would be a texture nothing here could read, and a faithful copy of the release's storage would be an image no kernel in this port can walk. So the class builds, the methods return an image of the requested shape, and the read count is carried, reads back and IS decremented by a kernel that reads the temporary: CharonMPSConsumeReadCount in CharonMPS.h now answers for MPSTemporaryImage as MPSImage.h:1030-1036 says it should - 'each time a MPSTemporaryImage is read by a MPSCNNKernel -encode... method, its readCount is automatically decremented' - and it was NOT doing so before, the helper knowing only the matrix and vector temporaries. tests/backports/host/mpstemporary/run.sh measures it: a temporary at readCount 2 answers 2 after -setReadCount:2, one MPSImageConvolution encode that reads it answers 1 and the next answers 0, a plain MPSImage is left alone, and a plant of the helper without that case turns the run red. NOBODY recycles anything, which is what keeps the row inert rather than implemented.
entries.effect: the symbol exists and loads and nothing in this port applies it. What a caller reaches: an MPSTemporaryImage built from the descriptor it passed, of the right shape and the right pixel format, and -readCount / -setReadCount: which read and store what the caller left there. What a caller does NOT reach: the release's guarantee that the storage is reclaimed when the command buffer completes and released early once the read count falls to zero. The read count is honoured, so a caller that watches it sees the uses the release says it would see; what the count still cannot do is RECLAIM anything. A temporary image here is an ordinary MPSImage that stays alive as long as the caller holds it, so a caller that assumed the release's lifetime would keep more memory alive than it expected - never less, and never a wrong number. That is why this row is inert and not implemented: the API is here and the behaviour behind it is not

entries.reason: IMPLEMENTED, in MPSNNReduce12.m, and the walk is a CPU walk. What decides that the port could carry it at all is the release's own cache rather than the header: objc-inventory.lua over the 16.0 arm64e cache lists MPSNNReduceColumnMax in MPSNeuralNetwork with superclass MPSNNReduceUnary and 3 instance selectors, none of them an encode, so the walk is the one it INHERITS from MPSCNNKernel - and MPSCNNKernel is a class this port already carries (MPSCNNKernel10.m, cnn.json, introduced 10.0, implemented), whose own -encodeToCommandBuffer:sourceImage:destinationImage: walks the image on the CPU exactly as MPSCNNPooling10.m's and MPSCNNConvolution10.m's do. MPSNNReduce.h:201 carries MPS_CLASS_AVAILABLE_STARTING(macos(10.13.4), ios(11.3), macCatalyst(13.0), tvos(11.3)), whose ios() clause reads ios(11.3). The axis and the operation are the header's own per-class sentence and not this port's arithmetic. The read window is MPSNNReduce.h:31-42's clipRectSource, which "replaces the MPSCNNKernel offset parameter for this filter. The latter is ignored" and is INTERSECTED with the image, default MPSRectNoClip. The walk itself is the one MPSImageReduceUnary16.m already performs for the MPSImageReduce classes over the same CharonMPSImageReadRegion / CharonMPSImageLoad / CharonMPSImageWriteRegion helpers, with the third axis MPSNNReduce names and MPSImageReduce does not added. Measured: 185 elements compared against a plain C reference written from the header's own wording, in the same process, with 0 mismatches; min, max and sum are compared for EQUALITY because they select or add values the source holds, and mean within one whole float32 ulp because it divides. Three mutations of this object - a column run starting at a row's stride, a feature-channel run walking pixels as well as channels, and the weight's default not being the header's 1.0 - each make the run red, so the comparison can fail. host MPS cannot run here, so no number on this row is a measurement of Apple's code: this host's AGX family lacks computeCommandEncoderWithDispatchType: and the release's own kernel dies encoding with '-[AGXG16XFamilyCommandBuffer mtlnext computeCommandEncoderWithDispatchType:]': unrecognized selector. What the rows say instead is the header's sentence, and the destination's SHAPE - which the header fixes the count of and never states - is the shape the count forces and is recorded as such rather than claimed as measured
entries.effect: the kernel is HERE and it computes: -encodeToCommandBuffer:sourceImage:destinationImage: walks the source on the CPU and writes the largest value of each column of each feature channel into the destination, so a caller that encodes gets numbers and not a texture. The count of answers is the header's own sentence - one per row, one per column, one per pixel - and the destination is that shape; where a row or column reduction carries the channel it reduced is decided from MPSCNNKernel's own sourceFeatureChannelOffset, since an MPSImage's row is a row of ONE feature channel, and that is stated here rather than claimed to be the release's measured layout. This class declares no `weight`: MPSNNReduce.h:413-420 puts the property on MPSNNReduceFeatureChannelsSum alone, and the release's own cache agrees - only that class among the twelve lists -weight and -setWeight: - so a weight has nothing to reach this walk through and the source's own values are what it combines. A destination too small for that count is refused BY NAME with the numbers in the message and nothing is written, because a write past the edge of a texture is what the release asserts on; the differential exercises it and the case prints the value that survived

entries.reason: IMPLEMENTED, in MPSNNReduce12.m, and the walk is a CPU walk. What decides that the port could carry it at all is the release's own cache rather than the header: objc-inventory.lua over the 16.0 arm64e cache lists MPSNNReduceColumnMean in MPSNeuralNetwork with superclass MPSNNReduceUnary and 3 instance selectors, none of them an encode, so the walk is the one it INHERITS from MPSCNNKernel - and MPSCNNKernel is a class this port already carries (MPSCNNKernel10.m, cnn.json, introduced 10.0, implemented), whose own -encodeToCommandBuffer:sourceImage:destinationImage: walks the image on the CPU exactly as MPSCNNPooling10.m's and MPSCNNConvolution10.m's do. MPSNNReduce.h:307 carries MPS_CLASS_AVAILABLE_STARTING(macos(10.13.4), ios(11.3), macCatalyst(13.0), tvos(11.3)), whose ios() clause reads ios(11.3). The axis and the operation are the header's own per-class sentence and not this port's arithmetic. The read window is MPSNNReduce.h:31-42's clipRectSource, which "replaces the MPSCNNKernel offset parameter for this filter. The latter is ignored" and is INTERSECTED with the image, default MPSRectNoClip. The walk itself is the one MPSImageReduceUnary16.m already performs for the MPSImageReduce classes over the same CharonMPSImageReadRegion / CharonMPSImageLoad / CharonMPSImageWriteRegion helpers, with the third axis MPSNNReduce names and MPSImageReduce does not added. Measured: 185 elements compared against a plain C reference written from the header's own wording, in the same process, with 0 mismatches; min, max and sum are compared for EQUALITY because they select or add values the source holds, and mean within one whole float32 ulp because it divides. Three mutations of this object - a column run starting at a row's stride, a feature-channel run walking pixels as well as channels, and the weight's default not being the header's 1.0 - each make the run red, so the comparison can fail. host MPS cannot run here, so no number on this row is a measurement of Apple's code: this host's AGX family lacks computeCommandEncoderWithDispatchType: and the release's own kernel dies encoding with '-[AGXG16XFamilyCommandBuffer mtlnext computeCommandEncoderWithDispatchType:]': unrecognized selector. What the rows say instead is the header's sentence, and the destination's SHAPE - which the header fixes the count of and never states - is the shape the count forces and is recorded as such rather than claimed as measured

Measured: a weighted sum of {1, 10, -1, 0.5} at 0.5 answers 5.25 and not 2.625. The weight is declared on this class ALONE - of the twelve concrete classes the release's own cache gives -weight and -setWeight: to this one only - so the other eleven reduce the source's own values. A destination too small for that count is refused BY NAME with the numbers in the message and nothing is written, because a write past the edge of a texture is what the release asserts on; the differential exercises it and the case prints the value that survived

entries.effect: the base is HERE and it refuses to be built: -initWithDevice: logs that the abstract base must not be instantiated, names the twelve classes that may be, and returns nil. The release asserts ("Cannot directly initialize MPSNNReduceUnary") and takes the process with it; refusing by name is what the rest of this package does rather than aborting a caller that got the class wrong, and a caller that holds nil cannot encode. -initWithCoder:device: builds one, and which axis and operation it is then is the coder's business - the base keeps no default a caller could rely on

entries.reason: IMPLEMENTED, in MPSNNStates12.m, and that file is where the ladder puts it: `printf 'MPSCNNNormalizationMeanAndVarianceState\n' | python3 tools/cache-index/first-rung.py` answers 12.0, the same rung its header's clause reads. MPSCNNBatchNormalization.h:102 annotates the class ios(12.0) and :103 makes it MPSState's, which MPSState11.m carries. Its two members are the mean and the variance, each an id<MTLBuffer> (:105 and :110), from an initializer that takes them and a class method that allocates one per feature channel. No number in this row is a measurement of Apple's code and this band claims none: the release's own MPS cannot run on this host (its AGX family lacks computeCommandEncoderWithDispatchType:, so the release's own kernel dies encoding, which facts/MetalPerformanceShaders/Image9.md records). What was measured is in the facts page with the commands beside it: the armv7 build of this package's MPS directory (clang 23.1.1 -c -fobjc-arc -fvisibility=hidden -target armv7-apple-ios6.0 -isysroot the 16.4 iPhoneOS SDK -Wall over all 74 of its .m files, 0 failures) and ld -r -undefined dynamic_lookup over those 74 objects, which leaves no MPS class undefined - the only _OBJC_* symbols left open are ten framework classes (NSObject, NSArray, NSMutableArray, NSMutableData, NSNull, NSNumber, NSString, NSValue, NSObject's metaclass and MTLTextureDescriptor). That is a PARTIAL link over one directory and not a dylib link. No host case, no device run and no gate.
entries.effect: the class is here: -mean and -variance answer, -initWithMean:variance: holds the two buffers as strong ivars, and +temporaryStateWithCommandBuffer:numberOfFeatureChannels: makes two shared buffers of that many floats and puts both in MPSState's resource list, which is what makes the state answer -resource and -bufferSizeAtIndex: for them. What fills the two buffers is the batch normalization gradient, which is ios(11.3) and is another slice's object; this class allocates what the header says it allocates and the row does not claim a mean or a variance is computed.

Four semantics the release's own answers settled and the header's prose alone got wrong here first, each measured in tests/backports/host/mpsndarray/run.sh and written into the facts page: the storage is PACKED and the 16-byte row is an ALLOCATION size, not an address (-resourceSize of a [2,3,4,5] float32 array answers 960 = 16 bytes a row over 3*4*5 rows while the element at (1,2,3,4) is at 1+2*2+3*6+4*24); -lengthOfDimension: on a descriptor reads THROUGH the permutation, so a transposed [2,3] answers 3 for dimension 0, while a transposed VIEW of a [2,3] array answers 2, the array's own shape, which MPSCore/MPSNDArray.h:235-237 permits; a slice changes the packed walk and not the shape, so a view of a [3,4,2] array sliced on dimension 1 reads its twelve values out of a view whose shape says twenty-four; and a nil strideBytes array means PACKED, which is a different number from the storage stride.
